questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Amsterdam have a great reputation as a good law school. Also, Amsterdam is a wonderful city to be a student in!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Mostly easy. All major issues like housing, enrolment in classes, etc. was settled before i left for Amsterdam.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: N/A.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had an easy time getting housing as i applied through the University. However, people who tried to find housing themselves experienced lots of trouble. Some had to stay in emergency accommodation, some moved around every month, and it was almost always significantly more expensive, and worse located. recommendation from my: Pay the application fee €100-ish, and apply for housing through UvA! Finding housing on your own in Amsterdam is stressfull and border-line impossible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Check the location, and see how far it is from Uni/the city. Some student-housing is located quite far away. be aware that you might have to use public transport everyday to get to school/into the city. If you look for housing on your own/private renting, a rent of €900 per month, is not uncommon.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there is a pre-registration, and then an actual registration/confirmation. remember to do both!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online help, and the exchange-student helpdesk are extremely helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: prepare in due time, and make sure you know all the classes you want to take. be careful at planning them! UvA works with 3 blocks instead 2 as we are used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The amount of reading is double what i was used to at UCPH. also, the courses are much more academic! be prepared to read a lot of scholarly articles, which might not always be easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: more academic, less practical.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Consumer Rights in the Digital Single Market
International law, introduction
International Trade Law
International Investment Law
International Commercial Arbitration

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International Commercial Arbitration. Great course, and even better educators! This course takes a lot of work, as there are weekly submissions, and twice the reading amount as used to, but the learning outcome is great!
International Investment Law. Extremely interesting class! Great learning outcome, and great educators. would recommend if you would like a combination of business-law and procedural law!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs per say. However, prepare for spending a lot on fun, activities, cafes, restaurants, trips etc., as Amsterdam and The Netherlands have a lot to offer.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and restaurants are a bit cheaper than Denmark. Besides that, the prices a roughly the same, tilting to the "a bit cheaper" side.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN is a club for international student, and they also host an intro week. If you want to meet other internationals from across study-programs, i recommend signing up.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on trips in the Netherlands and the rest of Europe. Train-tickets (if booked in advance) are significantly cheaper than Denmark, and Amsterdam is well-connected to other cities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips, see it all.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, the Dutch culture is very similar to Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Dutch students are, sadly, quite reserved. It is hard to become friends with them outside the classroom.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: they do not refrigerate their eggs in the supermarket.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Borrels (meaning beer with friends in the afternoon).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare well in advance. As soon as you know you want to go, write down all deadlines. 
Treat finding housing like you would treat booking a ticket for Roskilde Festival. if you want the good/cheap/downtown housing you have to be fast!
Prepare for twice the reading amount you are used to!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends i made, and the city I got to live in.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting accustomed to the "dutch way" of teaching, doing exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
